Re: Appeal of pre-service denial — total ankle replacement, CPT 27702  
Date of denial: August 20, 2026  
Appeal deadline: February 16, 2027  

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request that Aetna overturn the denial and authorize the requested procedure.

Aetna’s publicly available Total Ankle Arthroplasty Clinical Policy Bulletin, policy number 0645, identifies CPT 27702 as “Arthroplasty, ankle; with implant (total ankle)” and states that CPT 27702 is covered when the policy’s selection criteria are met. The policy states:

“Aetna considers total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) using a Food and Drug Administration-cleared implant ... medically necessary when the following criteria are met.”

The submitted clinical records address the principal medical-necessity requirements as follows:

1. Arthritic or severely degenerated ankle  
The June 8, 2026 weight-bearing ankle radiographs show tibiotalar joint-space obliteration with subchondral cysts. These findings document severe degenerative change of the affected ankle. The requested procedure is intended to replace this severely degenerated ankle joint.

2. Pain and loss of mobility and function  
The patient has experienced 18 months of progressive ankle pain that has not been relieved by rest. Examination documents range of motion limited by pain and positive provocative testing on the affected side. The patient walks with an antalgic gait and is limited to approximately two blocks. These findings establish clinically significant pain, loss of mobility, and functional impairment.

3. Conservative treatment has failed  
The patient completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits focused on ankle strengthening and balance over 10 weeks, from May 11, 2026, through July 20, 2026. This treatment is documented in the physical-therapy discharge note. The patient also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on May 8, 2026, provided only three weeks of partial relief. The records therefore demonstrate substantial conservative treatment without durable improvement.

The policy’s physical-therapy footnote states:

“Physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) must be recent (within the past year), for at least 6 weeks ... and needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history.”

The documented 10-week course of supervised physical therapy, including the discharge note, satisfies this duration and documentation requirement.

4. Absence of documented clinical concerns identified in the records  
The prior-authorization packet documents no active infection, a BMI of 29, and no untreated substance use. The records also do not identify a smoking-related concern. These findings support proceeding with ankle arthroplasty and do not provide a documented reason to deny the procedure.

The medical records supplied with this appeal should be reviewed together with the imaging, examination findings, physical-therapy discharge note, medication history, and injection history. If Aetna contends that a particular criterion remains unmet, please identify that criterion specifically and provide the clinical records and reasoning relied upon in making that determination. The denial letter does not identify which medical-necessity requirement was considered unsatisfied.

Please also confirm whether any additional information is required concerning skeletal maturity, the proposed implant’s FDA clearance, diabetes or HbA1c status if applicable, ankle alignment, bone quality, ligament stability, vascular status, or any other contraindication listed in policy 0645. If any such issue was the basis for the denial, please state it explicitly so that the treating surgeon can respond.

Based on the documented severe ankle degeneration, disabling pain and functional loss, failure of prolonged conservative treatment, and the absence of a documented contraindication in the submitted records, I request reversal of the denial and approval of CPT 27702.

Please send the appeal determination in writing. I also request a copy of the complete clinical-review criteria applied to this case, the specific criterion or criteria found unmet, the clinical rationale for the denial, and the records relied upon by the reviewer.

Sincerely,

Cameron Carter
